blocks.text: Condo buildings in Capitol Hill
Alto on Capitol Hill — 5535 Hastings Street

A 4-storey mixed-use woodframe low-rise at Hastings & Ellesmere (presale source, secondary). The presale record describes 20 luxury condominiums plus 11 live-work units (31 homes) and states completion in 2023; the building directory records 36 units, a 2024 build year, restrictions of pets allowed with restrictions and rentals allowed with restrictions, and amenities of central air conditioning, elevator, in-suite laundry and wheelchair access. The unit-count (31 vs 36) and year (2023 vs 2024) conflicts between the two sources are noted, not resolved — confirm against the strata plan and Form B.
Beta — 4721 Hastings Street

Built 2015 (building directory, secondary source, and current listings agree). Current listings describe a boutique building in the Heights near Confederation Park, with elevator and garage parking; a top-floor listing notes 11-foot vaulted ceilings. Unit count, construction and published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Altezza — 4710 Hastings Street

Built 2012 (current listings). A current listing for a 2-bedroom unit records pets allowed ("Pets, Yes" in the listing fields), 9-foot ceilings and North Shore mountain views, and a listing Q&A names the building Altezza. Unit count, construction and published rental/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Cedarwood — 5340 Hastings Street
A named building in the building directory with an active listing history at this address; the directory page was verified to exist for this building and address.
Saturna — 5988 Hastings Street

A listing index records a unit at this address as built in 1993. Unit count, construction and the strata's published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED — the townhouse-style entrances mean form should be confirmed against the strata plan before the building is quoted as pure apartment stock.
Centrale — 4488 Hastings Street (presale; boundary-flagged)

By First Track Development at Willingdon Ave & Hastings St: a boutique collection of 34 modern 1- and 2-bedroom homes with air cooling and elevator, per current presale listings, which record the build year as 2028 (i.e. future completion) and a presentation centre at 3776 Hastings St. As a presale, REDMA applies to developer contracts; assignment terms and restrictions are UNCONFIRMED until the disclosure statement is read.
Streets, schools and getting around Capitol Hill

items.t: Capitol Hill is a City of Burnaby hilltop neighbourhood on the north side of Hastings Street in North Burnaby, centred on Capitol Hill Reservoir Park at 229 N Hythe Ave. "Capitol Hill" is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the neighbourhood spans the summit north of Hastings Street, between the Vancouver Heights / Heights Urban Village streets to the west and Parkcrest to the east — exact MLS boundary streets are UNVERIFIED.
Every verified apartment building in is a Hastings Street address.

SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: Burnaby-wide Condos & Townhomes median was $686,000, $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market in September 2026. There is no Capitol Hill sub-area median.

Main streets: Hastings Street is the main east–west road below the hill; Willingdon Avenue runs south to Highway 1, Metrotown and BCIT; Holdom Avenue and Fell Avenue climb the hill's residential grid.

Transit anchors: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings Street below the hill, linking Burrard Station in downtown Vancouver with SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus, at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak; on September 7, 2026 TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, serving the Heights at the hill's west side. There is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Capitol Hill

items.t: Burnaby tax timing: City of Burnaby 2026 property taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% after the September due date. Strata owners pay through their own tax notice; at Kensington Gardens the maintenance fee itself includes property tax, per listings — a co-ownership tell, not a strata feature.

blocks.text: Good to know about Capitol Hill

items.t: The biggest "condo" complex on the hill is not a condo. Kensington Gardens holds 125 of the units a portal would count as Capitol Hill condos, and it is undivided-interest co-ownership from the mid-1960s — strip it out and the sub-area's true strata apartment stock is five small Hastings Street buildings plus one presale.

The R2 extension is dated September 7, 2026. TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue on that date, serving the Heights at the hill's west side and replacing the peak-only 222 bus — Hastings condo transit copy written before that date understates the service.

The west-edge presale wears two sub-area names. Centrale (4488 Hastings Street) is marketed by its developer as Capitol Hill and filed by listing feeds under Willingdon Heights; Strawhomes records the same split for its units (sub-area Willingdon Heights, complex Centrale, build year 2028). Which sub-area a portal assigns changes the comparables a buyer sees.

Alto's live-work units blur the condo count. Eleven of the homes in the presale record for 5535 Hastings Street are live-work units, not pure residential condominiums — one reason the presale count (20 condos + 11 live-work) and the directory count (36 units) do not reconcile on their face.

The hill's civic cluster is mid-decision. The Confederation Park Community Centre replacement — a 3-level facility that would retain the McGill Branch library (4595 Albert Street) and the Eileen Dailly pool (240 Willingdon Avenue) and replace the 1971 seniors centre — has been deferred by the City, and in August 2026 the Province funded 20 new before- and after-school child care spaces by repurposing school space at Confederation Park Elementary at the hill's west side.

The community hall predates the strata era. The Capitol Hill Community Hall, built 1947–1948 on a triangular lot in Dynes Park adjacent to Hastings Street at the terminus of the Hastings streetcar line, is on the City's heritage register — the Hastings frontage the condos now line was a streetcar terminus before it was a condo corridor.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Capitol Hill
Hilltop Greene — 368 Ellesmere Avenue. STRATA

Listings describe "a boutique collection of 32 luxurious townhomes" in Capitol Hill: a current listing records Sub-Type Townhouse, 2 storeys, built 2009, frame-wood construction with fibre-cement siding, with complex amenities of Bike Room, Trash, Maintenance Grounds, Hot Water, Management, Sewer and Snow Removal — a managed strata complex in form and operation. Tenure basis stated plainly: no mirror checked publishes a Title to Land field or strata plan number for this complex, so the plan number is UNCONFIRMED and the strata classification rests on the managed-complex listing evidence above plus the townhouse sub-type — confirm the plan and Title on the Form B before quoting either. Unit count 32 is as the listings state it. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED — confirm on the Form B.
Capitol Hill (building-directory name) — 388 Ellesmere Avenue. STRATA

A 5-unit townhouse strata two doors from Hilltop Greene: a current listing for unit 1 describes a "SPACIOUS 3-BEDROOM, 3-BATHROOM TOWNHOME" in a "BOUTIQUE 5-UNIT STRATA," and the building directory carries the address as a building named "Capitol Hill" with a Townhouse product variant, 5 units, amenities Bike Room and In Suite Laundry. Tenure basis: the listing's express "5-UNIT STRATA" statement plus the directory building record; strata plan number UNCONFIRMED. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED — confirm on the Form B.
Cassia (Guildford Brook Estates) — 6965 Hastings Street. STRATA — MIXED FORM (townhomes + garden flats in one complex). SUB-AREA CONFLICT FLAGGED (see headnote)

A November 12, 2010 Burnaby NewsLeader development report describes Guildford Brook Estates Inc.'s Cassia as "a distinctive collection of 60 garden flats and townhomes located at the foot of Burnaby Mountain," with 23 floorplans and every home carrying its own front door ("These are not condos, even though there are some one-level plans"). Current listings split the forms exactly as built: townhouse units are classified Sub-Type Townhouse / Row / Townhouse (unit 42, built 2011, own entrance, 2 parking) and garden-level units Sub-Type Apartment (unit 8, built 2010, at "Cassia"). Build-year conflict: listings show 2010 (unit 8) and 2011 (units 32, 42) by unit/phase — no single project year is published as settled. Published pet position: a unit listing records "2 Dog or 2 Cats allowed" (listing data — confirm on the Form B). Published rental/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Streets, schools and getting around Capitol Hill

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: not on the hilltop, which is detached houses on a sloping, view-oriented grid, but at the hill's base and east edge — the Ellesmere Avenue pocket just south of Hastings (Hilltop Greene; the 388 Ellesmere strata) and the Hastings Street foot-of-Burnaby-Mountain end (Cassia).

Main streets and transit: Hastings Street is the main east-west road below the hill; Willingdon Avenue runs south to Highway 1, Metrotown and BCIT; Holdom Avenue and Fell Avenue climb the hill's residential grid, and Ellesmere Avenue carries the townhouse pocket. The R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs along Hastings Street below the hill, linking Burrard Station in downtown Vancouver with SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus, at least every 10 minutes at peak and 15 minutes off-peak; on September 7, 2026 TransLink extended the R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue. There is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area.

Schools: Capitol Hill Elementary (K–7) on Holdom Ave is the in-area SD41 school on the Province's school list, and Burnaby North Secondary, 751 Hammarskjold Drive, is the North Burnaby secondary school. SD41 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Capitol Hill

items.t: Form B diligence (all 3 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. There is no Form B at Kensington Gardens — it is undivided-interest ownership, not strata. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.

blocks.text: Good to know about Capitol Hill

items.t: The biggest attached complex on the hill is not a strata at all. Kensington Gardens holds 125 of the units a portal would count as Capitol Hill attached homes, and it is undivided-interest co-ownership from the mid-1960s — strip it out and the sub-area's true townhouse stock is two small Ellesmere Avenue stratas plus Cassia at the mountain's foot.

Two townhouse stratas share one short street. Hilltop Greene (368 Ellesmere, 32 homes, 2009) and the 5-unit strata at 388 Ellesmere (2010/2011) sit on the same block south of Hastings — a buyer comparing "Ellesmere townhouses" is comparing a 32-unit managed complex against a 5-unit boutique strata with entirely different CRF and depreciation-report risk, at the same address stem.

Cassia was marketed as "not condos" in 2010. The development-era report stresses every home has its own front door and there is no lobby entrance — which is why its one-level garden flats still classify as Apartment in MLS while the multi-level homes classify as Townhouse, inside one strata.

The west-edge apartment presale wears two sub-area names. Centrale (4488 Hastings Street) is marketed by its developer as Capitol Hill and filed by listing feeds under Willingdon Heights, with a recorded build year of 2028. Which sub-area a portal assigns changes the comparables a buyer sees — the same filing split that affects Cassia at the east edge.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Capitol Hill
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established hillside house lots: The upper streets around Capitol Hill Reservoir Park are the view pocket; the flatter grid streets toward Willingdon Heights are the family pocket.

Lot character, as the research states it: typical lot sizes are UNVERIFIED at sub-area level — no official source read states them, and the research warns hillside lots vary by street. The only lot-size figures a source states are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: 280 m² and 281 m². Slope is the lot character that matters here, and it is documented as a diligence item, not a statistic.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel on Capitol Hill is confirmed in the research; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community — Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined only. SnapStats has NO land category, and no detached figure is a land figure. September 2026 context only: Capitol Hill sub-area detached inventory 40 / solds 3 (8% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" 18 / 3 (17%); Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and attached median $686,000. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only).

blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: No bare-land strata plan on Capitol Hill was verified: Stated plainly for any future claim: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure in BC — Form B, strata fees and bylaws apply — and no plan here has been shown to be one.
Kensington Gardens — 5740 / 5760 / 5770 Hastings Street. EXCLUDED, not land and not strata
Cassia — 6965 Hastings Street. Cross-reference only: It is built strata product, not a lot offering, and adds no land count here.

blocks.text: Development proposal

items.t: 4269 Hastings Street (Heights, below the hill): a six-storey mixed-use project — 37 non-market rental and strata homes over about 2,900 sq ft of ground-floor retail — has passed second reading. It is a rezoning-stage proposal for homes, not a lot sale, and nothing in it is for sale as land on this evidence.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Capitol Hill

items.t: Nearby areas: Vancouver Heights and the Heights Urban Village to the west and south-west, Willingdon Heights to the south, Parkcrest to the east, Lochdale and Montecito further east along Hastings.

Main roads and transit: Hastings Street runs east–west below the hill; Willingdon Avenue runs south to Highway 1, Metrotown and BCIT; Holdom Avenue and Fell Avenue climb the residential grid. TransLink's R5 Hastings St RapidBus links Burrard Station (downtown Vancouver) with SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus at least every 10 minutes at peak; on September 7, 2026 TransLink extended the R2 RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station via Hastings and Willingdon. There is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic cluster: Confederation Park, 250 Willingdon Avenue, at the hill's west end, with the Eileen Dailly Leisure Pool & Fitness Centre at 240 Willingdon Avenue and the McGill Branch library at 4595 Albert Street. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, south of the hill.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, with no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. The in-area Ministry-listed school is Capitol Hill Elementary (K–7) on Holdom Ave; Burnaby North Secondary is at 751 Hammarskjold Drive. One completed SD41 locator run is documented: for 4715 Pandora St (range 4715–4787 Pandora St), Confederation Park Elementary and Alpha Secondary — the west-side secondary catchment here is Alpha, not Burnaby North. Every other catchment is UNVERIFIED — check the exact address in the locator.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Capitol Hill

items.t: Slope and heritage diligence: no area-wide flood construction level for the Capitol Hill slope was identified in the City sources read; parcel-level slope, geotechnical and hazard status for individual hill lots is UNVERIFIED — budget a geotechnical check into any hillside lot purchase. The Capitol Hill Community Hall (built 1947–1948, on a triangular lot in Dynes Park at the Hastings streetcar terminus) is on the City's heritage register — a reminder to check heritage status before assuming a Hastings-edge lot is a clean teardown.

ALR rules (for completeness — no ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

blocks.text: Good to know about Capitol Hill

items.t: The hill's biggest "condo" complex holds no strata lot at all (documented 2026): Kensington Gardens' 125 units are undivided-interest co-ownership from the mid-1960s, and its maintenance fee itself includes property tax per listings — a co-ownership tell, not a strata feature. Strip it out and the hill's attached market is a handful of small Hastings buildings plus Cassia at the mountain's foot.

The R2 arrived on a dated day — September 7, 2026: TransLink extended the R2 RapidBus from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown via Hastings and Willingdon that day, replacing the peak-only 222 bus. Hastings-edge lot copy written before that date understates the frequent-transit position that feeds the R1 400 m / 6-unit test.

A deferred civic project sits at the hill's west end: the City's Confederation Park Community Centre replacement (3 levels beside the Eileen Dailly pool and McGill library at Willingdon and Albert, retaining the pool and library and replacing the 1971 seniors centre) is a City capital project the City states has been deferred — do not price a west-end lot off a promised new centre.

Child care is coming to a school at the hill's west side (announced August 2026): the Province funded repurposing school space at Confederation Park Elementary for 20 new before- and after-school child care spaces — small, dated, and exactly the kind of family-infrastructure fact Hastings-village marketing rarely mentions.

Page-statement check for this area. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Capitol Hill address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. Capitol Hill Elementary (K–7) on Holdom Ave is the in-area SD41 school and Burnaby North Secondary (8–12), 751 Hammarskjold Drive, is the North Burnaby secondary school; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

faq.q: How do I get downtown or to SFU without a car?
faq.a: The R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs below the hill on Hastings Street, connecting Burrard Station (downtown Vancouver) and the SFU Burnaby Mountain campus, running at least every 10 minutes at peak times; since September 7, 2026 the R2 also runs along Hastings and down Willingdon Avenue to Metrotown Station.

faq.q: What is at the top of Capitol Hill?
faq.a: Capitol Hill Reservoir Park, 229 N Hythe Ave — a small City park listed as a scenic viewpoint park, above the Confederation Park civic cluster of pool, community centre and McGill library branch at Willingdon and Albert.

faq.q: What did homes sell for recently on Capitol Hill?
faq.a: SnapStats does not publish a sub-area median for Capitol Hill. At the Burnaby community level, the September 2026 median sale price was $1,825,000 for detached and $686,000 for condos & townhomes; within Capitol Hill itself, 3 detached homes and 3 attached homes sold that month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Is Kensington Gardens a condo complex I can buy into like any strata?
faq.a: No. Listings state the ownership is undivided interest ownership: the complex (5740 / 5760 / 5770 Hastings Street, 7 three-storey buildings on 5.15 acres, 125 units per the directory's market report) is a co-ownership, not a strata corporation — no Form B, no strata depreciation report, and the maintenance fee includes property tax, heat and hot water. It files under "condos" in search feeds, which is exactly the trap.

faq.q: So what is Capitol Hill's actual strata apartment stock?
faq.a: A short Hastings Street list: Alto on Capitol Hill (5535 Hastings, 2023/2024), Beta (4721 Hastings, 2015), Altezza (4710 Hastings, 2012), Cedarwood (5340 Hastings, details UNCONFIRMED) and Saturna (5988 Hastings, recorded 1993), plus the Centrale presale at 4488 Hastings at the west edge.

faq.q: Why do sources disagree on Alto's size and year?
faq.a: The presale record describes 20 condominiums plus 11 live-work units (31 homes) in a 4-storey woodframe low-rise, completed 2023; the building directory records 36 units and a 2024 build year. Both are secondary sources — the strata plan and the Form B settle unit count and registration, and a buyer should quote neither figure as final until then.

faq.q: Can I rent out an Alto unit long-term?
faq.a: The directory records "rentals allowed with restrictions," and independently of any bylaw wording, strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. A short-term rental restriction can still bind — read the registered bylaws in the strata package.

faq.q: Are pets allowed in the Hastings buildings?
faq.a: Published positions differ by building: Alto — pets allowed with restrictions (directory); Altezza (4710 Hastings) — a current listing records pets allowed; the 6965 Hastings townhouses — a listing records 2 dogs or 2 cats allowed. For Beta, Cedarwood and Saturna, pet rules are UNCONFIRMED from public sources — pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC, so read the registered bylaws before writing.

faq.q: What townhouse complexes actually exist on Capitol Hill?
faq.a: Three verified strata complexes: Hilltop Greene (368 Ellesmere Ave, 32 townhomes, built 2009), the 5-unit townhouse strata at 388 Ellesmere Ave (directory name "Capitol Hill," built 2010/2011 — year UNCONFIRMED), and Cassia (6965 Hastings St, 60 homes mixing townhomes and garden flats, built 2010/2011 by unit).

faq.q: Is Kensington Gardens a townhouse or condo complex I can buy into like any strata?
faq.a: Neither, in the strata sense. Listings state the ownership at 5740 / 5760 / 5770 Hastings Street is undivided interest ownership: 7 three-storey buildings on 5.15 acres, 125 units per the directory's market report, but a co-ownership, not a strata corporation — no Form B, no strata depreciation report, and the maintenance fee includes property tax, heat and hot water. It files under attached product in search feeds, which is exactly the trap.

faq.q: Cassia — is it in Capitol Hill or Sperling-Duthie?
faq.a: A comp search run under only one sub-area name will miss listings filed under the other.
